dateline: Mexico City — ARMY Packs CDMX Ahead of GNP Seguros Opener Tomorrow; Jungkook 'Seven' Breaks Asian Billboard All-Time Record
heroHeadline: Day 4,710: BTS In Mexico City — Estadio GNP Seguros Opener Tomorrow; Jungkook's 'Seven' Sets New Asian Global 200 Record
heroSubtitle: May 6, 2026 is Day 4,710 since BTS's June 13, 2013 debut. ARMY from across Latin America is converging on Mexico City ahead of the ARIRANG World Tour's first show at Estadio GNP Seguros tomorrow (May 7) — with additional nights on May 9 and 10. The Mexico City run is BTS's first in the city since their 2019 Speak Yourself tour. Billboard charts for the week of May 9 confirm 'SWIM' is in its sixth consecutive week on the Hot 100 (No. 32) and No. 2 on the Global 200 for six straight weeks — the longest sustained K-pop top-tier Global 200 run ever. ARIRANG holds at No. 5 on the Billboard 200 (week 6). Separately, Jungkook's solo single 'Seven' reached its 142nd consecutive week on the Billboard Global 200 and 145th on Global excl. US — new Asian all-time records on both surveys. HYBE founder Bang Si-hyuk remains under a travel ban as South Korean police weigh re-filing an investor fraud arrest warrant following prosecutors' April 24 rejection.
footerNote: Data sourced from HYBE, Billboard, Hanteo Chart, Gaon Chart, Melon, Spotify, Guinness World Records, IFPI, Korea Times, Korea Herald, Yonhap, Bloomberg, Variety, AP News, UPI, STARNEWS Korea, Rolling Stone, Digital Music News, Deadline, Music Business Worldwide, Infobae Mexico, Milenio, Live Nation, and allkpop.
